ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.33 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted off-route segment on this metered RydeTAXI trip; record the RD-1 breach; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI job, so kilometres driven enter the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies: the total of $49.37 includes a distance component of $34.42 for 24.41 km [F6], and the excess distance was billed at this trip's own rate of $1.4101/km (distance fare ÷ distance km) [F4][RD-2].

One off-route segment exists: 09:24–09:30, where 3.78 km were driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 0.71 km, adding 3.07 km and straying up to 688 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. Neither advocate disputes that this is the only deviation, and the whole-trip delta of +3.2 km / +8.4 min [F1][F2] is that same event.

No exemption applies. The complete chat record — two timestamped messages, the rider's 09:04 pickup description and the driver's 09:05 arrival note [F7][F8][F9] — contains no rider request for a stop or a route, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt (no rider-named place, and no stop was measured in the segment). Similarly there is no rider message before 09:24 agreeing to a route, whether general or naming a road, so RD-5 gives no consent; the driver's post-trip statement that "the GPS sent me; it rerouted" [F10] is a claim only and cannot supply rider agreement (G11) [RD-5]. RD-4 fails as well: no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F13], the only speed records are band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard, outside the band 1–2 requirement [F11][F12][RD-4], and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain [F14]. The segment therefore counts as an unexempted detour.

Amount: RD-2 refunds Σ extra_km of unexempted segments × this trip's per-km rate, and expressly does not refund the difference between fare-excess and the sum of the segments. The segment adds 3.07 km, so 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.3290 → $4.33 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The rider's requested $4.51 rests on the whole-trip excess of 3.20 km [F4], and its own 0.13 km residue is not tied to any segment (corridor jitter/noise), which RD-2 excludes.

No account flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, and the profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (the one upheld dispute is a no-show) [F16][RD-6]. Profile facts are not used to decide the deviation itself [F15][F16].

segment_findings.reason: The chat record is complete and shows only the rider's 09:04 pickup description and the driver's 09:05 arrival note, both before the 09:24 segment start, so no rider message agrees to this route or to any stop; the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim, not rider consent (G11). No RD-3(a) rider-named stop and no RD-4 incident exist either. The segment is an unexempted off-route segment and its extra km are refundable [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-1][RD-2][RD-3][RD-4][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider asks for the whole billed excess of $4.51 (3.20 km), but RD-2 refunds only Σ extra_km of unexempted segments × the per-km rate and expressly does not refund the difference between fare-excess and the segment sum; the segment adds 3.07 km [F3], giving 3.07 × $1.4101 = $4.33 [F3][F4][RD-2].

RD-6's flag_account condition requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the profile records 0 (the one upheld dispute is a no-show), so no account action arises and profile facts cannot decide the deviation [F16][RD-6].

The driver's long clean history and 0 upheld route disputes are not a defence to the measured deviation; profile facts never decide the case, and RD-6 is only an additional-action ground [F15][F16][RD-1][RD-6].

The driver concedes the GPS-reroute statement [F10] cannot exempt the segment; I agree — a post-trip statement is not rider consent (G11) and names no traffic cause, so it fails both RD-4 and RD-5 [F10][RD-4][RD-5].
